Okay, here's the full known-good state: sensor A's signal wire (yellow) goes to A0, red to 3V, black to GND — same for sensor B into A1. The board runs power→sensor→number→rule→output in that order, so if the number never changes, the break is almost always the sensor-to-board connection, not the code.

If you've checked all five — power on, sensor number changing, verdict flipping at your line, buzzer firing on manual trigger, and the sequence running in order — and it's still dead, use restore and rebuild the wiring fresh rather than hunting further. This exact spot catches nearly everyone, so don't feel bad about it.

calls.answer:
Power test first: plug in, and check whether the display lights up at all with any number showing — even a wrong one. If nothing lights up, the fault's between the board and the display, so check that the DSP wire is actually seated in the DSP pin, not slipped one pin over onto DIAL or RING.

If the display does light up, move to the sensor test: warm sensor A with your hand on A0 and watch if the number on the display moves at all. Tell me what you actually see happening right now — lit or dark, number moving or stuck — so we know which of the two checks you're in.
